description: What build 1.0.0 (5) sends to the server and how it reads each answer, recorded from its app code at the tag builds/1.0.0/5. The server must keep giving every answer below as this build reads it, until the release guide retires the build. Never edit this folder: the server changes by adding, and make server-check fails on an edit.

stops.shape: a stop area with a number of 5 digits, as a metro or RER line of the station list asks
a stop area with a number of 6 digits
a quay, as a metro line with no stop area asks

answers.reads: the times: any 2xx status, Last-Modified in the one form that the build parses, and the PRIM answer as PRIM gave it; no-store keeps the system cache of the phone from giving an old answer again

answers.when: the calls of the hour are spent, and the server holds a recent answer of the stop
the calls of the hour are spent
answers.reads: the server is out: the build shows no live times until the retry time, and asks again only then
the server is out, as above
a failure of this stop: the build shows Times unavailable, and asks this stop again only after the retry time; any reason but budget and prim-limit reads this way

answers.when: the server does not accept the app token
answers.reads: the refusal: this build reads the status 401 and the error unauthorized together as Update the app, and makes no call until the app is opened or a Live Activity starts; another 401, or a 403, is a failure like any other; other keys may join the body

stations.shape: a station number of 5 digits, as most metro stations of the station list
a stop place of 5 digits, as most RER stations of the station list

startTokens.shape: 32 bytes in lowercase hex, the size of a device token
80 bytes in lowercase hex: the build sends the start token of ActivityKit at the length that iOS gives it

answers.when: Apple's push service takes the start
answers.reads: the start: status 200 with the result started or already-started; the build then does nothing more, and the Live Activity comes by itself; other keys may join the body

answers.when: the same start token asks again for the same station, a moment after the start
answers.reads: the start, as above: iOS often gives the build the same arrival twice

answers.when: Apple's push service says that the start token is not valid
answers.reads: no start, and the build drops this start token, so that no later ask uses it: status 502 with the result refused and the reason BadDeviceToken (no service of Apple knows the token) or Unregistered (the token is no longer active); other keys may join the body

answers.when: Apple's push service refuses the channel of the station
answers.reads: no start, and the build keeps its start token: any status but 200 is no start, whatever the body says, and the body is a JSON object whose reason, if any, is neither BadDeviceToken nor Unregistered, which would make the build drop a token that works; nothing else comes, and no arrival notification

answers.when: Apple's push service refuses the start for a reason that is not the start token
answers.reads: no start, and the build keeps its start token, as above: the same token may start the Live Activity at the next station

answers.when: Apple's push service does not answer
answers.reads: no start, and the build keeps its start token, as above

answers.when: the server has no push key of Apple
answers.reads: no start, and the build keeps its start token, as above

answers.when: the server does not accept the app token
answers.reads: no start, and the build keeps its start token, as above: on this route, this build shows no Update the app for a refused token
